title: Xenotopic Synthetic Biology: Engineering Non-Natural Metabolic Pathways for Production of Rare Bioactive Compounds in Microbial Hosts
abstract: We developed a xenotopic synthetic biology framework for expressing non-natural metabolic pathways in microbial hosts to produce rare bioactive compounds. Using directed evolution of enzyme cascades, we produced 23 novel curcuminoid analogs with improved bioavailability and anti-inflammatory activity compared to natural compounds.

sections.Research Question: Can xenotopic synthetic biology—engineering non-natural metabolic pathways in living organisms—produce novel bioactive compounds with improved pharmacological properties that are inaccessible through natural product isolation or traditional organic synthesis?This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing available evidence from multiple sources to establish a comprehensive understanding of the research problem.
sections.Search Summary: Literature review in PubMed and Web of Science for xenobiotics, synthetic biology, directed evolution, and bioactive compound production through December 2025.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Traditional natural product drug discovery is limited by compound availability from natural sources. Synthetic biology offers a complementary approach but has been largely confined to optimizing naturally occurring biosynthetic pathways. Xenotopic approaches that introduce entirely non-natural metabolic logic represent an emerging frontier.
sections.Key Findings: The xenotopic framework enabled production of 23 novel curcuminoid analogs with improved bioavailability (3.2-fold higher plasma concentrations vs natural curcumin) and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity (IC50 0.8 uM vs 3.2 uM for natural curcumin) [bundle:1]. The approach used directed evolution to optimize enzyme cascades for non-natural substrate specificity [bundle:2]. Scale-up to 100L fermentation achieved yields of 2.3 g/L for the lead analog.
sections.Limitations: Only curcuminoid analogs were demonstrated; generalizability to other compound classes requires further development. Regulatory pathway for xenotopic-produced compounds is undefined.
sections.Gaps Identified: Expansion of the xenotopic framework to other bioactive compound classes including alkaloids, terpenoids, and polyketides. Development of regulatory frameworks for xenotopic natural products.
sections.Conclusion: Xenotopic synthetic biology represents a powerful new approach for producing novel bioactive compounds with improved pharmacological properties inaccessible to traditional discovery methods.

title: Organism-Wide Cellular Dynamics and Epigenomic Remodeling During Natural Aging in Non-Human Primates
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics across 9 organs in 48 cynomolgus monkeys spanning ages 3-30 years revealed cell-type-specific aging programs, progressive immune infiltration of barrier tissues, and shared epigenetic drift patterns across cell types resembling epigenetic aging clocks.

sections.Research Question: What are the cell-type-specific and organ-wide aging programs operating across the primate lifespan, and to what extent do different tissues share common versus unique aging signatures?This systematic investigation addresses gaps in current knowledge by synthesizing available evidence from multiple sources to establish a comprehensive understanding of the research problem. sections.Search Summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing, ATAC-seq, and multiome analyses across 9 organs in 48 cynomolgus monkeys from 3 to 30 years of age.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Single-cell aging studies in primates have been limited by tissue accessibility and cost. Most aging atlases have been built in mice, with limited primate data.
sections.Key Findings: Cell-type-specific aging programs were identified in each organ, with the most pronounced changes in immune cell populations [bundle:1]. Progressive immune infiltration of barrier tissues (lung, gut, skin) was observed across all animals. Shared epigenetic drift patterns across cell types correlated with chronological age and matched epigenetic clock predictions [bundle:2].
sections.Limitations: Captive primate population may not fully reflect natural aging trajectories. Cross-sectional design cannot capture individual aging trajectories.
sections.Gaps Identified: Longitudinal single-cell profiling in individual primates across the lifespan would enable within-individual aging rate estimation.
sections.Conclusion: Primate aging involves both cell-type-specific programs and organism-wide epigenetic drift patterns, providing a mechanistic bridge between mouse aging studies and human aging.

title: TRIALSCOPE: Clinical Trial Simulation from Real-World Data Using Causal Machine Learning for Counterfactual Prediction
abstract: We developed TRIALSCOPE, a causal machine learning framework that generates realistic simulated clinical trial populations from electronic health record data. Counterfactual predictions of treatment effects were validated against 12 completed randomized trials, showing good calibration and high discrimination for treatment responders.

sections.Search Summary: Review of causal machine learning, clinical trial simulation, and real-world evidence methods in PubMed through December 2025.
sections.Evidence Landscape: Synthetic control arms and trial simulation from real-world data have been proposed to reduce trial costs and improve efficiency, but methods for generating realistic counterfactual outcomes have been limited.

abstract: We present updated global obesity prevalence data and a systematic review of emerging pharmacological interventions.
